options: Cash that has been refunded to a customer
Money from a known customer that hasn't been matched to a specific transaction yet
A journal entry created during period close
Cash collected through a lockbox that failed validation
questions.explain: Unapplied cash is tied to a known customer but has not yet been applied against any specific open transaction.

questions.q: How does on-account cash differ from unapplied cash?
options: On-account cash is always a larger dollar amount
On-account cash is formally a standing credit on the account with no particular invoice in mind, rather than cash awaiting a match
On-account cash can only come from miscellaneous receipts
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: On-account cash is a deliberate standing credit on the customer's account, while unapplied cash is expected to be matched to a transaction soon.

questions.q: Does unapplied or on-account cash automatically close an open invoice?
options: Yes, both automatically close the oldest open invoice
No, an invoice remains open until someone performs the application
Only on-account cash closes invoices automatically
Only unapplied cash closes invoices automatically
questions.explain: Neither unapplied nor on-account cash closes an invoice by itself — the open balance remains until a clerk applies the cash against it.

questions.q: Why is it risky for a collections team to work strictly off the aging report without checking for unapplied or on-account cash?
options: The aging report never includes real customer data
They might chase a customer for a late payment who is actually sitting on a credit that covers it
The aging report only shows paid invoices
Aging reports cannot be run while receipts are unapplied
questions.explain: Open invoice balances on an aging report don't reflect idle credits, so a customer could look delinquent while actually holding cash that covers the balance.

questions.q: What is a common business reason on-account cash arises?
options: A customer makes a prepayment ahead of an expected order
A bank rejects a receipt for insufficient funds
A transaction is reversed in error
A customer disputes a credit memo
questions.explain: A deliberate prepayment with no specific invoice yet to apply against is a typical source of on-account cash.
